meta.title: Hávamál
meta.numbering: Neckel 1914, 164 stanzas. Brate 1913 uses the same numbers. Bellows 1923 is mapped onto them.
meta.on: Gustav Neckel, Edda: Die Lieder des Codex Regius nebst verwandten Denkmälern, I. Text (Heidelberg: Winter, 1914), pp. 16–43. Public domain. Half-lines that Neckel prints on one line with a caesura are broken onto their own lines here. Wording, punctuation, lacuna dots, and editorial marks (†, *) are unchanged.
meta.en: Henry Adams Bellows, The Poetic Edda (New York: The American-Scandinavian Foundation, 1923), Hovamol. Public domain. Text from Project Gutenberg ebook 73533. The caesura bar in that transcription is a line break here. Wording is unchanged. Bellows’s introduction and notes are not included.
meta.sv: Erik Brate, Eddan: De nordiska guda- och hjältesångerna (1913), “Den höges sång”. Public domain. Electronic text from Project Runeberg (runeberg.org/eddan/se-02.html), as digitized. Wording is unchanged.

stanzas.theme: Look around before you enter
en: Full long let him look about him;
And sit in the seats within.

stanzas.theme: A guest has come in
sv: skall fresta, vad framgång han får.
en: The proof of his might to make.

stanzas.theme: Fire, food, and clothes
on: þeim er hefir um fiall farit.
sv: och kall har blivit om knäna.
en: Has come from the cold without;
The man from the mountains come.

stanzas.theme: Water, welcome, and talk
en: Should he find who comes to the feast;
Wisely and well must he act.

stanzas.theme: Wits for the one who wanders
en: But all is easy at home;
When among such men he sits.

stanzas.theme: Do not boast of your mind
en: But keep it close in his breast;
When he goes as guest to a house;

stanzas.theme: The guest who watches and listens
sv: så spanar var klok och spejar.
en: Thus wary are wise men all.

stanzas.theme: Praise you win for yourself
en: That is hid in another’s heart.

stanzas.theme: Wisdom in your own breast
No better burden than sense
en: And in grief a refuge it gives.

stanzas.theme: Ale is poor provision
The more you drink, the less you master
sv: vet till sig, vad tankar han har.
en: Of his mind the mastery hold.

stanzas.theme: The heron of forgetfulness
sv: han snattar från män deras sans.
en: And steals the minds of men;
And in Gunnloth’s house was held.

stanzas.theme: Drunk at wise Fjalar’s
en: When with Fjalar wise I was;

stanzas.theme: Silent, wise, and brave until death
en: And bold in battle as well;
Till the day of his death is come.

stanzas.theme: The coward does not escape age
sv: om för vapenskifte han sig aktar,
en: If the fight he faces not;
But age shall not grant him
Though spears may spare his life.

stanzas.theme: The fool at the feast, once he drinks
sv: han talar om allt eller tiger;
då är det slut med hans slughet.
en: when he comes to the feast,
He stammers or else is still;
What the mind of the man is like.

stanzas.theme: Only the wide traveler knows minds
Drink in measure, then go to bed
on: at þu gangir snemma at sofa.
sv: tala, vad som höves, eller tig!
en: Speak to the point or be still;
If soon thy bed thou seekest.

stanzas.theme: The greedy belly
en: Will eat till sick he is;
To scorn by his belly is brought.

stanzas.theme: The herds know when to go home
en: And then from the grass they go;

stanzas.theme: The man who mocks everything
sv: gör hån åt vad som helst;
en: That he is not free from faults.

stanzas.theme: The fool awake all night
sv: grubblar och grämer sig för allt;
en: And his woe is just as it was.

stanzas.theme: The fool thinks the mockers are friends
on: þótt þeir um hann fár lesi,
en: Who laugh at him will hold;
Though hatred of him they speak.

stanzas.theme: At the assembly he has few to speak for him
en: Who laugh at him will hold;
But the truth when he comes
That few in his favor will speak.

stanzas.theme: Alone, the fool thinks he knows all
on: ef hann á sér í vá vero;
sv: när i vrå i skygd han vistas;
en: When he sits by himself in a corner;

stanzas.theme: Best for the fool to keep silent
on: þat er batst, at hann þegi;
sv: gör bäst i att tyst förbliva;
om ej för ymnigt han ordar.
om icke för ymnigt han ordar.
en: If his mouth is not open too much.
When his mouth has been open too much.)

stanzas.theme: Wise, who can ask and tell it again
sv: som går ifrån mun till mun.

stanzas.theme: The tongue that never rests
en: With words that win no faith;
if a bridle it find not,

stanzas.theme: Do not hold another up to mockery
sv: om han gör som gäst besök.
en: Although he fare to the feast;

stanzas.theme: The guest who takes to his heels
sv: en gäst, som är hånfull mot gäst.
om han med gramsne ej glammar.
en: When mock of another he makes;
Though he mocks in the midst of his foes.

stanzas.theme: Friends who fall out over a feast
en: Till feasting they mock at their friends;

stanzas.theme: Eat early, or sit and say nothing
sv: om han till bekanta ej kommer;
en: Nor fasting come to the feast;
And little is able to ask.

stanzas.theme: A long road to a foe, a short one to a friend
sv: fast vid vägen hans stuga stode;
en: is the road to a foe,
Though his house on the highway be;
is the way to a friend,

stanzas.theme: Do not sit forever as a guest
sv: på en annans bänk han bliver.
en: By the hearth in another’s home.

stanzas.theme: Better a small home than begging
on: þat er þó betra en bœn.
sv: Fast man tågor har till tak
är det bättre än bedja om mat.
en: A man is master at home;

stanzas.theme: Better a home than having to beg for food
en: A man is master at home;
When food he fain would have.

stanzas.theme: Do not walk a foot from your weapons
en: A man should fare not a foot;
when the need for a spear
Shall arise on the distant road.

stanzas.theme: No host so free that a gift was unwelcome
on: at leið sé laun, ef þægi.
sv: att ej åt gåvor han gladdes,
att led vore lön, om han finge.
en: That gladly he took not a gift,
That of recompense hatred he had.

stanzas.theme: Do not save for a foe what a friend needs
sv: mycket går värre, än man väntat.
en: Let him never suffer in need;
Oft he saves for a foe
what he plans for a friend,
For much goes worse than we wish.

stanzas.theme: Gifts make the longest friendships
on: ef þat bíðr at verða vel.
sv: om annars det vill sig väl.
en: As each for himself can see;
If fair their fates may be.

stanzas.theme: Repay a gift with a gift, a mock with a mock
sv: och försök att lura med lögn.

stanzas.theme: Be a friend to your friend, and to his friend
en: To him and the friend of his friend;
With one of his foeman’s friends.

stanzas.theme: Go often to the friend you trust
on: ok vill þú af hánom gott geta:
sv: Vet du, om vän du har,
och gott av honom vill hava;
en: And good from him wouldst get,
And fare to find him oft.

stanzas.theme: Speak fair to the one you do not trust
on: vildu af hánom þó gott geta:
sv: och av honom dock gott vill hava;
en: Yet good from him wouldst get,

stanzas.theme: Laugh with him, and do not open your mind
on: ok þér er grunr at hans geði:
sv: och vars onda sinne du anar:
en: And whose mind thou mayst not know;
Like gifts to his shalt thou give.

stanzas.theme: Young and alone, rich when a companion came
sv: då råkade jag vilse om vägen;
en: And nought of the road I knew;

stanzas.theme: The brave live best; the coward is afraid
en: And not gladly the niggard gives.

stanzas.theme: Clothes made two wooden poles look like heroes
en: To a pair of carven poles;
But the naked man is nought.

stanzas.theme: A man unloved, like a fir on a bare hill
sv: och ej skyddas av bark eller barr;
en: All bootless its needles and bark;
Why should his life be long?

stanzas.theme: False friendship burns out in five days
en: And ended is all the love.

stanzas.theme: Half a loaf and a half-full cup won a friend
on: opt kaupir sér í litlo lof:
sv: ofta får han lovord för litet;
en: A friend full fast I made.

stanzas.theme: Small seas, and minds that are not all alike
en: And small are the minds of men;

stanzas.theme: A measure of wisdom, and not too much
en: But never too much let him know;

stanzas.theme: Too much wisdom, and a heart seldom glad
on: ef sá er alsnotr, er á.
sv: om allvis han är, som det äger.
en: But never too much let him know;
If wisdom too great he has won.

stanzas.theme: Do not see your fate before it comes
en: But never too much let him know;
For so is he freest from sorrow.

stanzas.theme: A brand kindles a brand; speech shows the man
sv: och den alltför slöe genom slapphet.
en: And the stupid by their stillness.

stanzas.theme: The idle wolf and the sleeper win little
en: Or the goods of another would get;

stanzas.theme: Rise early when few work beside you
on: ok ganga síns verka á vit;
sv: och tage med sin syssla i tu!
en: For the swift is wealth half won.

stanzas.theme: Know the wood and bark a season needs
en: For the thatch let one know his need,
he must have for a month,
Or in half a year he will use.

stanzas.theme: Washed and fed, to the assembly
on: þótt hann sét væddr til vel:
en: But care not too much for thy clothes;
Less still of the steed he rides,
(Though poor be the horse he has.)

stanzas.theme: The eagle, and the man with few to speak for him
en: He snaps and hangs his head;
in the midst of a throng,
Who few to speak for him finds.

stanzas.theme: Tell one person; what three know, all know
sv: veta det tre, så vet världen.
en: Who wish to be known as wise;
All know what is known to three.

stanzas.theme: Use your strength in measure
sv: att ingen är djärv framför alla.
en: Of the might he has will make;
That the boldest he may not be.

stanzas.theme: Words spoken to others often come back bitter
sv: som till andra man har sagt,
en: He will get but an evil gift.
stanzas.svNote: Brate prints only the lines that remain. The lost opening is the dotted lines in the Old Norse and in Bellows.

stanzas.theme: Too early, or too late, and the ale was wrong
en: And some too late have I sought;

stanzas.theme: Welcome everywhere, had only one ham been eaten
sv: om ej mat till målen jag behövt,
en: To their homes men would bid me
If at meal-time I needed no meat,
Where only one I had eaten.

stanzas.theme: Fire, the sun, health, and a life unstained
en: And power to see the sun;
if a man may have it,
And a life not stained with sin.

stanzas.theme: Not wholly wretched: sons, kin, wealth, or deeds
sv: mången av fullt upp med gods,
en: Some from their sons have joy,

stanzas.theme: Better to live than to lie a corpse
on: en úti var dauðr fyr durom.
sv: vid liv, får sig karl alltid ko.
och död låg han utanför dörren.
en: The live man catches the cow;
And before his door he lay dead.

stanzas.theme: The lame can ride; a corpse is of no use
sv: ej av någon nytta är liket.
en: The deaf in battle is bold;
No good can come of a corpse.

stanzas.theme: A son is better, though born late
sv: om ej frände över frände dem rest.
en: And his father to death have fared;
Save when kinsman honors his kin.

stanzas.theme: Two are an army; the tongue slays the head
Glad of the night who has food; weather turns
en: (Short are the yards of a ship,)
And more in a month’s time.

stanzas.theme: Riches make many a fool; do not scorn poverty
sv: av rikedom mången röjes som narr.
lägg ej den det till last!
en: Yet scorn for him none should know.

stanzas.theme: Cattle die, and kinsmen die; a good name does not
sv: för envar, som ett gott har vunnit.
en: And so one dies one’s self;

stanzas.theme: Cattle die; the judgment on each dead man does not
en: And so one dies one’s self;
The fame of a dead man’s deeds.

stanzas.theme: Fitjung’s sons: wealth blinks, and is gone
sv: nu traska de med tiggarens stav.
en: Now bear they the beggar’s staff;
Of friends the falsest it is.

stanzas.theme: Wealth or a woman’s love swells a fool’s pride
on: fram gengr hann driúgt í dul.
sv: i dårskap går han duktigt långt.
en: Or wealth he chances to win,
Straight forward he fares in conceit.

stanzas.theme: Asked about the runes, silence is safest
on: þá hefir hann batst, ef hann þegir.
sv: om de stavar, som från gudarne stamma,
då tyckes det bäst, att han tiger.
en: That the gods so great have made,

stanzas.theme: Praise the day when evening has come
sv: gift kvinna, då hon bränd är,
en: Give praise to the day at evening,
to a woman on her pyre,
To a weapon which is tried,
To ice when it is crossed,

stanzas.theme: Cut wood in a wind; talk with a maid in the dark
sv: I blåsväder skall skog man fälla,
i bris ro ut på öppet hav,
Å skepp skall man fart göra
en: When the gale blows hew wood,
in fair winds seek the water;

stanzas.theme: Ale by the fire; buy a lean horse and a dull sword
sv: Vid eld skall man öl dricka,
en kamp skall man mager köpa,
en: Buy a steed that is lean,
stanzas.svNote: The Project Runeberg text has “kamp” and “höst” in this stanza. Beside it, the Old Norse is a lean horse, fattened at home. The Swedish is kept as that electronic edition prints it.

stanzas.theme: Do not trust a maiden’s words
sv: eller tro på gift kvinnas tal;
en: Nor the word a woman speaks;
For their hearts on a whirling
And fickle their breasts were formed.

stanzas.theme: No trust in a breaking bow, a flame, or a wolf
No trust in an arrow, new ice, or a serpent
No trust in a sick calf or a stubborn thrall
en: In a calf that is sick

stanzas.theme: Do not trust an early-sown field, or a son too soon
sv: och ej för snart sin son;
en: Nor trust too soon in thy son;

stanzas.theme: A brother’s killer, a half-burned house, a swift horse
sv: att han litar på allt detta!
en: as to trust in them all.

stanzas.theme: Fickle love, like a horse unshod on ice
sv: är som med häst utan broddar
eller som halt man på töfjäll

stanzas.theme: Men’s minds fail women, as women’s fail men
sv: karlars tro mot kvinnor även vacklar.
en: Men false to women are found;
Against wisdom we work with deceit.

stanzas.theme: Fair speech and a gift, to win love
on: sá er vill flióðs ást fá,
sv: om en flickas kärlek man vill få,
en: Who longs for a maiden’s love,
He wins whose wooing is best.

stanzas.theme: Do not blame another man for falling in love
Do not blame a fault that many share
on: þess er um margan gengr guma:
en: For what touches many a man;

stanzas.theme: No sickness worse than to be pleased with nothing
on: einn er hann sér um sefa:
sv: än att leva, med intet belåten.
en: A man knows his mind alone;
Than to lack the longed-for joy.

stanzas.theme: Waiting in the reeds for the one I wanted
on: þeygi ek hana at heldr hefik.
sv: för att möta min älskade mö;
och dock jag ingenting av henne fick.
en: when I sat in the reeds,

stanzas.theme: Billing’s daughter asleep, bright as the sun
on: nema við þat lík at lifa.
sv: mot att med denna förlederska leva.
en: In slumber bright as the sun;

stanzas.theme: Come back at evening, Óðinn
on: ef þú vilt þér mæla man;
sv: om mö di dig vinna vill;
en: If a woman thou wouldst win;
Should know of such a sin.”

stanzas.theme: I turned away sure that joy was certain
sv: vist var ej, vad jag ville.

stanzas.theme: The whole guard awake, with burning lights
on: svá var mér vilstígr of vitaðr.

stanzas.theme: At morning a bitch was tied on the bed
on: er ek var enn um kominn,

stanzas.theme: Many a good maid turns, if you test her
on: ok hafða ek þess vetki vífs.
sv: lätt ändrar sitt lynne mot män.
och intet jag fick av den flickan.
en: if a man but tries them,
False to a lover are found;
And nought from the woman I won.

stanzas.theme: Glad at home with guests, and wary all the same
on: heitir, sá er fátt kann segia:
sv: Man skall glad i hemmet vara.
dock förståndigt man sörje för sitt;
en: A man shall be wary and wise;
Must see that his speech be fair;
For such is the way of the witless.

stanzas.theme: I sought the old giant, and I have come back
on: nú em ek aptr um kominn;
sv: där föga jag fick med att tiga.
en: Small gain from silence I got;

stanzas.theme: Gunnlǫð gave the mead from the golden seat
sv: en dryck av det dyrbara mjödet.
en: A drink of the marvelous mead;

stanzas.theme: Rati’s mouth, the way bored through the rock
sv: då gällde det hals och huvud.
en: And space in the stone he gnawed;
So rashly I risked my head.

stanzas.theme: The dear drink well used; Óðrœrir came among men
sv: dit, där människor bygga och bo.
en: To the midst of the men of earth.

stanzas.theme: I might not have come home without Gunnlǫð
sv: om ej av Gunnlod jag hjälpts,
som jag fick i famnen sluta.
en: Whose arms about me had been.

stanzas.theme: Next day the frost-giants asked for Bǫlverkr
on: ef hann væri með bǫndom kominn
eða hefði hánom Suttungr of sóit.
en: Some word of Hor to win,
were he back midst the gods,
Or had Suttung slain him there?

stanzas.theme: An oath on the ring, and Gunnlǫð left in tears
sv: Ed på ring tror jag Oden
hur kan man på hans löften lita?
och i gråt han lämnade Gunnlod.
en: Who now his troth shall trust?
And Gunnloth to grief he left.

stanzas.theme: Time to speak from the sage’s seat at Urðr’s well
sv: Om runor hörde jag dem tala,
om råd de ej heller tego,
en: By the wells of Urth I was,
And heard the speech of Hor.
Such was the speech I heard.)

stanzas.theme: Do not rise at night unless you must
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
eða þú leitir þér innan út staðar.
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
om du ej är ute och spanar
eller måste ut på gården gå!
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Or fain to the outhouse wouldst fare.

stanzas.theme: Do not sleep in a witch’s embrace
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
svá at hon lyki þik liðom.
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
så att hon i famnen dig fängslar!
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Nor let her limbs ensnare thee.

stanzas.theme: After her spell: no food, no joy, no good sleep
sv: om till ting eller konungen du kallas;
en: For the council or meeting of men;
And sadly to slumber thou farest.

stanzas.theme: Do not chase another man’s wife
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Or long for her secret love.

stanzas.theme: On a long way, look to the food you carry
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Look well to thy food for the way.

stanzas.theme: Let an evil man bring you nothing
on: Ráðomk þér, Loddfáfnir, en þú ráð nemir —
þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Bring aught of ill to thee;

stanzas.theme: A man wounded to death by a lying tongue
sv: genom ord av en ond kvinna;
och dock ej för sann sak.
en: And no word of truth there was.

stanzas.theme: Visit the friend you trust, or the path grows over
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
Vet, om en vän du har,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Then fare to find him oft;

stanzas.theme: Hold a good man in friendship
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
ok nem líknargaldr, meðan þú lifir.
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
lär dig tjusa folk att hålla dig kär!
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
And give heed to his healing charms.

stanzas.theme: Do not be the first to break with your friend
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
The bond that holds you both;

stanzas.theme: Do not trade words with a fool
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:

stanzas.theme: An evil man does not pay a good turn
sv: och gör dig omtyckt av andra.
en: Through words of praise will win thee.

stanzas.theme: Nothing is worse than to be false
on: era sá vinr ǫðrom, er vilt eitt segir.
sv: den är ej vän, som blott välkommet säger.

stanzas.theme: Do not argue even three words with a worse man
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
With a worse man speak not
When the worse man wields a sword.

stanzas.theme: If you make a shoe or a shaft, make it for yourself
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
If the shoe is ill made,
Then evil of thee men think.

stanzas.theme: Call evil evil, and do not befriend a foe
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
och giv ej din fiende frid.
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
And make no friendship with foes.

stanzas.theme: Take no joy in evil; let good make you glad
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
en lát þér at góðo getit.
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
But glad the good shall make thee.

stanzas.theme: Do not look up while the battle is on
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:

stanzas.theme: Want her love: promise fairly, and keep it
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
ef þú vilt þér góða kono
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
den blir glad, som får något gott.
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
None loathes what good he gets.

stanzas.theme: Be wary, not fearful: ale, a wife, a thief
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:

stanzas.theme: Do not mock a guest or a traveler
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Of a guest or a journey-goer.

stanzas.theme: No one who comes is only good, or only worthless
on: hvers þeir ro kyns, er koma;
né svá illr, at einugi dugi.
sv: vad slags folk, som farande komma.
eller så dålig, att till intet han duger.
en: What kind is the man who comes;
Nor so wicked that nought he is worth.

stanzas.theme: Do not scorn the grey singer; the old often speak well
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
opt er gott, þat er gamlir kveða,
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
ofta gott är, vad de gamle säga.
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Oft do the old speak good;
Though it hang with the hides,
And is blown with the bellies.)

stanzas.theme: Do not curse a guest, or show him the door
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
En gäst du skall ej skymfa
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:
Deal well with a man in want.

stanzas.theme: The beam that must open needs a ring
en: To give an entrance to all;
The wish it would work on thee.

stanzas.theme: When you drink ale, take the strength of the earth
on: þér muno góð, ef þú getr —:
sv: du får fördel, om du följer dem,
Då öl du dricker, sök hjälp
en: Profit thou hast if thou hearest,
Great thy gain if thou learnest:

stanzas.theme: I know that I hung on the windy tree
sv: av vad rot det runnit upp.
en: Hung there for nights full nine;
With the spear I was wounded,

stanzas.theme: No loaf was given, and no horn
Nine mighty songs, from Bǫlþorn’s famous son
on: nam ek af inom frægia syni

stanzas.theme: Word from word, deed from deed, I began to grow
en: I grew and well I was;

stanzas.theme: You will find the runes, and the great staves
en: That the king of singers colored,
And the mighty gods have made;
That the ruler of gods doth write.

stanzas.theme: Who cut runes for gods, elves, dwarfs, and giants
Do you know how to cut, read, color, ask, offer, send?
sv: Vet du, hur du rista skall?
Vet du, hur du reda skall?
Vet du, hur du färga skall?
Vet du, hur du fresta skall?
Vet du, hur du bedja skall?
Vet du, hur du blota skall?
Vet du, hur du sända skall?
Vet du, hur du slopa skall?

stanzas.theme: Better unasked than too great a sacrifice
en: By thy getting measure thy gift;

stanzas.theme: A song named Help
en: Nor men that are sons of men;
and help it can bring thee
In sorrow and pain and sickness.

stanzas.theme: Another song, for those who would be healers
A third: I blunt the edges turned against me
sv: att deras klingor och knölpåkar ej bita.
en: Of fetters to hold my foe;
Nor bites his sword or staff.

stanzas.theme: A fourth: I sing, and the fetters spring apart
en: The fetters spring from my feet,
Broken the bonds from my hands.

stanzas.theme: A fifth: I stop a shaft shot into the host
on: ef ek sé af fári skotinn
ef ek hann siónom of sék.
sv: om blott min syn honom sett.
en: If ever my eyes behold it.

stanzas.theme: A sixth: harm sent by a root turns on the sender
on: þann eta mein heldr en mik.
sv: genom runor på rötter av träd,
det blir menligt mera än för mig.
en: With a sapling’s roots to send me;
Shall taste the ill ere I.

stanzas.theme: A seventh: the hall burns, and I can quench it
on: þann kann ek galdr at gala.
sv: slik galder, som jag säga kan.
en: The hall o’er my comrades’ heads;
that I will not quench it,
I know that song to sing.

stanzas.theme: An eighth: I can settle hatred quickly
en: I soon can set it right.

stanzas.theme: A ninth: I quiet the wind and put the sea to sleep
on: at biarga fari míno á floti,
sv: att bärga min båt på hav;
och sjunger all sjö i sömn.
en: To shelter my ship on the flood;
And the sea I put to sleep.

stanzas.theme: A tenth: witches riding, I send them astray
sv: om själen, som de själva ha.

stanzas.theme: An eleventh: my friends go whole into battle and home
sv: komma helbrägda från vad som helst.
en: To the fight my long-loved friends;
Whole to the field of fight,
Whole from the field of fight,
And whole they come thence home.

stanzas.theme: A twelfth: I cut runes, and the hanged man speaks
on: ef ek sé á tré uppi
en: I see a hanged man swing;

stanzas.theme: A thirteenth: water on a young man, and he does not fall
sv: ej segnar denne krigare för svärd.
en: though he fares mid the host,

stanzas.theme: A fourteenth: I can tell gods and elves apart
sv: den ej kunnig är, det ej kan.
en: Few be the fools know this.

stanzas.theme: A fifteenth: Þjóðrørir sang before Dellingr’s doors
en: Of Delling sang Thjothrörir the dwarf;
Might he sang for the gods,

stanzas.theme: A sixteenth: I turn the mind of a wise woman
on: ef ek vil ins svinna mans
ok sný ek hennar ǫllom sefa.
sv: lidelse och lust jag vill hava.
en: To win from a maiden wise;
And thus change all her thoughts.

stanzas.theme: A seventeenth, and songs Loddfáfnir still lacks
on: þó sé þér góð, ef þú getr,
sv: Men de äro goda som gåva,
en: Well, if thou wouldst them learn,

stanzas.theme: An eighteenth, told to no woman but one
en: To maiden or wife of man,—
So comes the end of the songs,—
Or who else my sister is.

stanzas.theme: The High One has spoken his words in the hall
sv: Nu är den Höges sång framsagd
en: Kind for the kindred of men,
Cursed for the kindred of giants:
Profit be his who has them!
